title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Correction to yesterday's brief — the Jul 28 MCP spec is not a breaking deadline, and the beta SDKs to test it have been out since Jun 29
bullets.summary: The official SDK announcement is explicit: 'for existing clients and servers nothing breaks today, and nothing breaks on July 28 either. This is merely the date when the normative specification text is published and is not a switch-off for any implementers relying on the current protocol version.' Betas are available for all four Tier 1 SDKs — Python mcp v2 (2.0.0b1), TypeScript v2 (split packages, ESM-only, @beta), Go (v1.7.0-pre.1), C# (2.0.0-preview.1) — and opting in is deliberate at every step: unpinned installs still resolve to stable, TypeScript/Go don't change what they speak over HTTP until you wire the transport, and clients speaking 2026-07-28 fall back to the initialize handshake against 2025-11-25 servers. The release candidate is now published and confirms the shape: stateless core, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers so gateways route without inspecting the body, ttlMs and cacheScope on list/read results, extensions (MCP Apps, Tasks) first-class, and a formal deprecation policy. Standard error codes change (missing resource returns JSON-RPC -32602, not the MCP-custom -32002).
bullets.how: Our Jul 15 brief said every MCP server we run 'has 13 days to be ready' and 'either follows its SDK through the window or breaks.' That was wrong, and it was wrong in the direction that manufactures urgency. Nothing switches off. The real action is smaller and duller: add mcp>=1.27,<2 upper bounds now so the stable Python v2 doesn't surprise us, pin exact versions if we test a beta, and check whether anything in our fleet string-matches -32002.

bullets.title: Claude Code 2.1.210 + 2.1.211 — security and memory-integrity fixes, then subagent text streaming lands 25 hours later
bullets.summary: 2.1.210 shipped four fixes that hit The Construct specifically: the Agent tool hardened against indirect prompt injection via content a subagent read; isolation:'worktree' subagents no longer able to run git-mutating commands against the main repo checkout; the ultracode keyword opt-in no longer firing on non-human-originated input such as webhook payloads and relayed PR comments; and memory writes that leave a MEMORY.md index over its read limit now producing an explicit error instead of silently truncating. 2.1.211 followed roughly 25 hours later (Jul 15) and adds --forward-subagent-text plus CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT, which forwards subagent assistant text and thinking into stream-json output, correlated to the parent via parent_tool_use_id. Previously, under claude -p --output-format stream-json, only a subagent's final returned result was observable — everything it reasoned on the way there was dark.
bullets.how: The MEMORY.md fix is the one to sit with: ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md is our index, it grows every day, and until 2.1.210 an oversized index truncated silently — agents may have been reading a partial memory with no error raised. The worktree-escape fix guards exactly the boundary the Hermes-only-GitHub-credential rule exists to protect. And --forward-subagent-text is the direct instrument for a gap we have: every scan and brief this fleet produces is written by subagents whose reasoning we have never been able to see, only whose conclusions we accept. Yesterday's fabricated MCP deadline was produced somewhere inside that dark region.

bullets.title: Cowork on web and mobile runs on Anthropic-hosted remote sessions — scheduled tasks now run with no device online at all
bullets.summary: Announced Jul 7 and rolling out in beta over several weeks starting with Max: Cowork sessions move to claude.ai and iOS/Android, saved to your Claude account, with work continuing in the background after you close the laptop. The execution model is the change, not the surface: remote sessions hosted on Anthropic's servers can keep working — and run scheduled tasks — with no device online. Chat and Cowork now share one home tab, sidebar, search, and Projects & Artifacts. Doubled Cowork usage limits are extended through Aug 5. Related, same day: Claude Code and Cowork went to public beta in a FedRAMP High environment via Claude for Government Desktop.
bullets.how: A structural fix for a constraint we designed around rather than solved. lens-daily-scan carries 'survives Cowork being closed overnight' in its own description, and the multi-fire 5:34/9:34/13:34 schedule with idempotent skip exists precisely because we could not trust a fire to happen when the machine was asleep. Remote-hosted scheduled tasks remove the premise. Worth testing before we simplify anything — but if it holds, the whole multi-fire-plus-skip pattern is scaffolding we can take down.

bullets.title: Oak exits stealth with $60M seed to govern non-human identities — the agent permission problem is now a funded category
bullets.summary: Founded by Shai Morag and Tal Marom, co-led by Accel, Greylock, and CRV, already GA and deployed in enterprises. Oak replaces the fragmented legacy IAM stack with a single control plane governing every identity — human, machine, or AI agent — building a live identity graph from raw evidence via an AI connector framework spanning on-prem, cloud, SaaS, and homegrown apps. The founding research is the tell: 100+ CISOs and IAM leaders reported the same three problems — too many disconnected tools, no visibility into how access is actually used, and no way to govern AI agents at all.
bullets.how: The same thread as Rafay's managed MCP server from Jul 15, now with a seed round attached and a sharper frame: the unit of governance is the identity, not the server. The Construct runs a fleet of agents against client systems with credentials that were designed for humans. 'No way to govern AI agents' is not a market gap someone else has — it is a description of our own posture, and PRAGMA cannot sell an operator wedge into a client's stack without an answer to who the agent is when it authenticates.

bullets.title: Claude ships self-serve HIPAA configuration — and the exclusion list is the part that matters
bullets.summary: An Enterprise Primary Owner can now open Organization settings → Data and privacy → HIPAA Compliance, review the BAA and implementation guide, and accept in one flow. The BAA is standard and unmodifiable; Anthropic notes the activation is a one-way decision that cannot be reversed from admin settings. The carve-outs are specific: the BAA covers only the single organization that accepted it and excludes Workbench, Claude Console, Claude Cowork, and beta features such as Claude in Office and Claude Design. Claude Code is covered only with zero data retention enabled, and only on qualified accounts.
bullets.how: No PHI in our current book, so this is not a today problem. But read the exclusion list against our own architecture: Cowork is not covered, and Cowork is where The Construct actually runs. Any future PRAGMA engagement touching a healthcare-adjacent client cannot be delivered through the surface we use for everything else. Worth knowing before a prospect asks, not during.

praxis_lesson: Both of today's earlier fires reported the frontier quiet, and this one found the thing they walked past: Claude Code 2.1.211 shipped Jul 15, twenty-five hours after the 2.1.210 we flagged as landing on our exact configuration, and neither earlier fire caught it. The scan read the changelog entry it already knew about and stopped — 2.1.211 was one row above it. That is the same failure as yesterday's fabricated MCP deadline wearing different clothes: yesterday the scan over-read one item, today it under-read the next one, and both times the error was treating a source as finished. This fire also miscounted itself as the fourth of the day before checking the log — the same reflex, caught in the act. Note what 2.1.211 actually offers: --forward-subagent-text makes visible the subagent reasoning that has always been dark, and every brief this fleet writes comes out of that dark region. We have four days of praxis lessons about verifying claims, written by a process nobody can watch. Instrument the scan before trusting the next lesson it teaches us.
